title.narrative: MULTI-DIMENSIONAL RESILIENT RECOVERY OF THE IBO AND BUZI DISTRICTS

description.narrative: A joint effort through three key agencies (UN-Habitat, ILO and UNESCO) is instrumental to enhance a multi-dimensional project that tackles strategic actions to provide an inclusive, sustainable and resilient framework of action to kick-start reconstruction with a focus on supporting vulnerable populations and local authorities, in a general effort of piloting recovery solutions and implementation modalities defined by the Government of Mozambique - Reconstruction Cabinet in its Post Disaster Reconstruction Plan (PREPOC). A bottom-up approach with communities and households at the centre of the process, as well as CSOs and NGOs, interacting with local authority and implementing agencies, in a harmonized and coordinated way to pursue its goals. Economic, environmental and spatial analysis will be carried out to understand in which way each one of the two contexts should be tackled for the reconstruction based on the distribution of their functions, their influence on surrounding areas (urban-rural linkages), in order to plan and extend the concept of resilience to the surrounding environment. In addition, capacity analysis on local construction (heritage restoration, resilient local techniques, materials, etc.) and local production skills (agriculture, fishing, etc.) will provide the baseline for a tailor-made approach of the Project activities and the implementation of participatory methods. These will feed, in the first project component, the design of two Integrated recovery and reconstruction strategies at district level, with specific action plans for each territories and target neighbourhood, resulting from different types of interventions (Partial and Total Reconstruction, Retrofit, Integrated Recovery of Human Settlements-Existing or New/Resettlement) and operational procedures (“banco de materiais”, community contracts, electronic vouchers) defined by the Reconstruction Cabinet in the PALPOC (Post Disaster Housing Action Plan) and adapted to the particular contexts of Ibo and Buzi District. The first project component will begin during the inception phase, in each of the two districts, and will be strategic and transversal to the other three project components, creating the baseline and the shared agreement on priorities and intervention strategy, to serve at the same time the definition of a first Operational Plan for project implementation and the definition of the local recovery framework to be adopted by the district and the Reconstruction Cabinet. This strategy and action plans will be developed in a participatory manner, also following Reconstruction Guidelines, defining consultative bodies such the Local consultative Councils, as well as creating coordination platforms at local authority level, with the aim to implement area-based interventions for resilience building integrating various aspects simultaneously, i.e.: (i) access to basic services (health, education, water, sanitation, waste management) and infrastructure (drainage and roads); (ii) access to secure land tenure; (iii) nature-based solutions and improved public spaces; (iv) affordable housing development; (v) vocational training, income generation activities and/or job creation
